title: Large connectivity expansion of Ising Spin Glasses on random graphs
authors: Luca Maria Del Bono, Flavio Nicoletti, Federico Ricci-Tersenghi
abstract: We compute a high-connectivity analytical expansion for Ising spin glasses on sparse random graphs. We expand the cavity equations around the fully-connected mean-field limit, focusing on the critical behavior of the system: our approach allows us to compute the de Almeida-Thouless line of mean-field finitely-connected systems in the temperature $T$--magnetic field $H$ plane, by means of closed analytical equations. The exact cavity solution of such systems can only be obtained by solving numerically iterative equations, so our approach brings a notable computational advantage. On the theoretical side, we are able to identify three sources of corrections to the fully-connected mean-field solution: i) the non-Gaussianity of the cavity fields, ii) the statistical correlation between the cavity fields and their fluctuations, and iii) the corrections to the cavity filter functions. These corrections are treated using two different expansions: a non-uniform expansion, where we expand all three contributions around the mean-field solution, and a uniform expansion, where we only expand the statistics but leave the cavity filters untouched. The former allows for a direct comparison with the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model but fails at low temperatures, as a consequence of the de Almeida-Thouless line diverging in the zero-temperature limit. On the other hand, the uniform expansion describes with good accuracy the critical behavior of the system. We also extend these results to the $T = 0$ limit.
summary: This work develops a high-connectivity analytical expansion for Ising spin glasses on random graphs to study their critical behavior. By expanding cavity equations around the mean-field limit, the authors derive closed-form equations for the de Almeida-Thouless line. The uniform expansion proves particularly useful, offering accurate descriptions of the system's critical properties across a wide range of temperatures.
main_problem: The paper aims to compute a high-connectivity analytical expansion for Ising spin glasses defined on sparse random graphs, focusing specifically on determining the critical behavior of the system.
main_result: The authors derive closed analytical equations for the de Almeida-Thouless (dAT) line in the $T$-$H$ plane, providing a computational advantage over purely numerical methods for mean-field finitely-connected systems.
method: The primary method involves expanding the cavity equations around the fully-connected mean-field limit, utilizing two distinct approaches: a non-uniform expansion and a uniform expansion.
model_or_system: The system is the Ising spin glass defined on a Random Regular Graph with connectivity $c$. The Hamiltonian involves random couplings $J_{ij}$ (Rademacher variables) and external fields $a_i$.
key_observables: The de Almeida-Thouless (dAT) line in the temperature ($T$)–magnetic field ($H$) plane, and the critical behavior at $T=0$.
important_parameters: Connectivity $c$, temperature $T$, magnetic field $H$, and the branching ratio $b=c-1$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the high-connectivity limit ($c 	o \infty$) for the analytical expansion, and the uniform expansion is necessary to maintain accuracy across all temperatures.
figures_summary: Figure 1 compares numerically computed probability distributions $P(h)$ with the fully connected prediction, demonstrating convergence as connectivity $c$ increases.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the physical model and the cavity method framework, develops the high-$c$ expansion using two types of approximations (non-uniform and uniform), derives the analytical equations for the dAT line, and validates the results by extending the analysis to the $T=0$ limit.
why_interesting: While focused on classical statistical mechanics, the techniques developed—analytical expansions around mean-field limits and the study of phase transitions in disordered systems—are foundational to understanding complex quantum many-body systems, particularly those exhibiting glassy dynamics.

figures.caption: Figure 1. Comparison between the numerically computed (solid color lines) and the fully connected (dashed black line) P(h) (18), at H = 0.2 and T = 0.726, for values of the connectivity c ranging from 3 to 200. For increasing c, the curves tend to collapse one on top of the other and to approach the fully connected one. Data are obtained by running a Population Dynamics algorithm with N = 106 elements, thermalization time tth = 1000, total time ttot = 5000, and by taking one measurement every δt = 50 steps. Data were further averaged over R = 50 independent runs. Errors are smaller than the lines.
